lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner studies three provided fictional sample documents side by side and, for each, names what it proves, how long it's useful for, and the one or two details on it that would matter most in a later problem.
safetyNotes: All three documents are fictional samples provided with this lesson; no real transaction, business, or account is involved.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Why do you think people commonly lose or discard documents like these before they'd actually need them?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Distinguishing the three document types: Correctly explains what at least two of the three documents prove. | Identifying the details that matter: Names specific details and gives a plausible reason for at least two documents. | Reasoning about why documents get lost: Offers a plausible, non-judgmental reason. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner design a simple system (physical or digital) for keeping these kinds of documents for a set period, and explain why they chose that length of time for each type.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: a notebook or document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner studies three provided fictional sample documents side by side and, for each, names what it proves, how long it's useful for, and the one or two details on it that would matter most in a later problem.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for decision or action.

Model move 3: For each of the three sample documents, name what it proves and how long it stays useful.

Model check: Distinguishing the three document types: Correctly explains what at least two of the three documents prove. | Identifying the details that matter: Names specific details and gives a plausible reason for at least two documents. | Reasoning about why documents get lost: Offers a plausible, non-judgmental reason.

resources.title: what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner studies three provided fictional sample documents side by side and, for each, names what it proves, how long it's useful for, and the one or two details on it that would matter most in a later problem.
Coach direction: Before studying the samples, write what you currently think each of the three document types is for.
Learner prompt: Write your current guess at what a receipt, a warranty, and a confirmation are each for.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each of the three sample documents, name what it proves and how long it stays useful.
Response 1 (t2-p1): For the receipt, explain what it proves and for how long it would matter.
Response 2 (t2-p2): For the warranty, explain what it proves and for how long it would matter.
Response 3 (t2-p3): For the confirmation, explain what it proves and for how long it would matter.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Why do you think people commonly lose or discard documents like these before they'd actually need them?

Success checks: Distinguishing the three document types: Correctly explains what at least two of the three documents prove. | Identifying the details that matter: Names specific details and gives a plausible reason for at least two documents. | Reasoning about why documents get lost: Offers a plausible, non-judgmental reason.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional what a receipt, warranty, or confirmation is for condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Distinguishing the three document types: Correctly explains what at least two of the three documents prove. | Identifying the details that matter: Names specific details and gives a plausible reason for at least two documents. | Reasoning about why documents get lost: Offers a plausible, non-judgmental reason..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u04-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
